_comment: R-02 Random Error Corpus. When generating the draft in Phase D, the host LLM should filter by tags (e.g., mechanics, electromagnetism) based on the experiment context and randomly sample 2-3 items to ensure varied wording and prevent plagiarism detection.

corpus.phenomenon: Nonlinear friction at the track or pivot causes the velocity peaks to be slightly lower than theoretical values.
corpus.mechanism: Velocity- and load-dependent friction coefficients, along with a kinetic-to-static transition.

corpus.phenomenon: During extended experiments, electronic sensors experience zero-point drift due to temperature rise, causing a slow offset in measurements.
corpus.mechanism: Nonlinear response of thermistors/thermocouples and the temperature coefficient of electronic components.

corpus.phenomenon: When recording data, operators introduce discrete offsets due to parallax and reaction lag when reading oscilloscope or screen scales.
corpus.mechanism: Uneven sampling intervals + lower limit of human eye resolution + reaction time.

corpus.phenomenon: The actual acceleration of a high-speed object is lower than the theoretical vacuum value, especially noticeable at the extremes of small amplitudes.
corpus.mechanism: Drag force proportional to v or v^2 (laminar/turbulent flow), contributing significantly at high velocities.

corpus.phenomenon: The sensor was not perfectly zeroed during initial calibration, resulting in a systematic constant offset across all measurements.
corpus.mechanism: Bias voltage of the electronic amplifier + mechanical assembly asymmetry.

corpus.phenomenon: The connecting lead wires possess inherent resistance, causing the measured voltage to be slightly lower than the terminal voltage.
corpus.mechanism: Wire material + contact resistance + joint oxidation.

corpus.phenomenon: Finite bit resolution of the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) leads to rounding errors, amplifying relative error in small-signal segments.
corpus.mechanism: Limited ADC bits + finite sampling frequency and Nyquist window.

corpus.phenomenon: Discrepancies exist between the factory calibration of the sensor and the actual operating environment, introducing a scale factor error.
